newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan Bourse lifted by news of merger.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan Bourse lifted by news of merger.

text.p: The Casablanca stock exchange ended its two-hour session on Thursday up 0.24 points, boosted by news of the merger between one of the market's blue chips, Wafabank and the Spanish Uniban, stockbrokers said.
The all-share index closed at 437.15 from 436.08 points on Wednesday.

"There is no doubt that the news of the merger between Wafabank and Uniban made the index go up together with Credor, a stock newly listed on the Bourse," an analyst at Casablanca-based Maroc Inter Titres (MIT) said.
Wafabank said on Thursday it would buy 100 percent of the Spanish Uniban bank.
Final agreement will be sealed when Uniban's general assembly meets on December 30 and after approval by the monetary authorities.

Credit Domestic Rapide (CREDOR), a leading private firm, which floated 240,000 shares worth 92.4 million dirhams ($10.5 million) on the stock exchange at an offer price of 385 dirhams, jumped to 421 dirhams on Thursday from 409 dirham the day before.
First tranche of privatisation bonds issued in January dropped 31 dirhams to 1,100 dirhams.
"As no privatisation is scheduled soon, holders tend to sell their shares," the stockbroker said.
ONA Group, Morocco's largest private conglomerate, remained unchanged for the third session at 500 dirhams this week.
ONA has diversified stakes in more than 100 companies and a capitalisation of more than 8.3 billion dirhams.
Societe Nationale d'Investissment, the second largest conglomerate, was unchanged at 530 dirhams.
Traded volume on the official market was 22.1 million dirhams from 26.4 million on Wednesday.
